proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a support rule \(s\) and an index \(e=(j,h)\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} gives \(D_{jK}\ne\varnothing\), while the
definition of the adoption-time donor sets and \(h\leq K\) give
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\).  Thus \(\Delta(D^s_e)\) is nonempty under
either rule.  It is a compact simplex.  The map
\[
 q_e(\omega)=a_e(\omega)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_e(\omega) \tag{24}
\]
is continuous, so the minimum \(v_{s,e}\) is attained.  Because
\(\Sigma_Q\succ0\) and \(a_e(\omega)\ne0\), its focal-cell coefficient being
one,
\[
 q_e(\omega)>0\quad\text{for every }\omega\in\Delta(D^s_e),
 \qquad v_{s,e}>0. \tag{25}
\]

Under \(L=\delta=0\),
\texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} applies and gives
\[
 W_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}r_\alpha
 \!\left(A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\right). \tag{26}
\]
This equality follows there from
\(\widehat\tau(w)-\tau\), not from a redefinition of the potential-outcome
target \(\tau\).

For distinct \(e,f\in\mathcal E\), row \(a_e(w)\) is supported on
\(\mathcal C^s_e\) and row \(a_f(w)\) is supported on
\(\mathcal C^s_f\).  Pairwise disjointness of these sets and diagonality of
\(\Sigma_Q\) imply
\[
 a_e(w)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_f(w)=0. \tag{27}
\]
Consequently the centered Gaussian error covariance in (26) is diagonal,
with diagonal entry \(q_e(w_e)\) in coordinate \(e\).  Therefore, for every
\(R\geq0\),
\[
 \Pr\{\lVert Z(w)\rVert_\infty\leq R\}
 =\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt{q_e(w_e)}}\right)-1\right\}. \tag{28}
\]

Define
\[
 \Psi_s(R)=\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt{v_{s,e}}}\right)-1\right\}.
 \tag{29}
\]
The set \(\mathcal E\) is finite and nonempty and every \(v_{s,e}\) is
positive.  Hence \(\Psi_s\) is continuous and strictly increasing on
\([0,\infty)\), satisfies \(\Psi_s(0)=0\), and converges to one as
\(R\to\infty\).  Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\), there is a unique positive
\(R_s\) for which \(\Psi_s(R_s)=1-\alpha\).

For \(R>0\) and \(v>0\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dv}\left\{2\Phi(R/\sqrt v)-1\right\}
 =-Rv^{-3/2}\varphi(R/\sqrt v)<0. \tag{30}
\]
Every feasible coordinate weight satisfies \(q_e(w_e)\geq v_{s,e}\).
Equations (28)--(30) therefore show that at any fixed positive \(R\), the
largest feasible cube probability is \(\Psi_s(R)\).  Because
\(\mathcal F_s\) is the Cartesian product of the coordinate simplexes, this
upper bound is attained by choosing, independently for every \(e\), a weight
that attains \(v_{s,e}\).  Thus the minimum in (26) equals \(R_s\), proving
\[
 W_s=R_s
\]
and the product-root characterization (8).

Now suppose the displayed subclass conditions hold for both support rules.
For every \(e=(j,h)\),
\[
 D^{\mathrm{deep}}_e=D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}
 =D^{\mathrm{nested}}_e,
\]
so minimization of the same quadratic (24) over the two simplexes gives
\[
 v_{\mathrm{nested},e}\leq v_{\mathrm{deep},e}
 \qquad(e\in\mathcal E). \tag{31}
\]
Let \(\bar w_D\) and \(\bar w_N\) collect coordinatewise
variance-minimizing weights under the deep and nested rules, respectively.
The product argument above proves that \(\bar w_D\) is a deep minimizer in
(26).  Equations (27) and (31) give
\[
 V(\bar w_N)=\operatorname{diag}
   (v_{\mathrm{nested},e}:e\in\mathcal E)
 \preceq
 \operatorname{diag}
   (v_{\mathrm{deep},e}:e\in\mathcal E)
 =V(\bar w_D). \tag{32}
\]
If (31) is strict for at least one coordinate, the two matrices in (32) are
unequal.  The strict covariance criterion in
\texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} then yields
\[
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{33}
\]
All compactness and positivity statements are finite-dimensional; no rank
condition on predictors, interiority of a simplex minimizer, boundary
regularization, or asymptotic limit is used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\).  Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and symmetric about the origin, and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) be integrable, symmetric, and have convex superlevel sets.  Then, for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(0\leq k\leq1\),
\[
 \int_C f(x+ky)\,dx\geq \int_C f(x+y)\,dx.
\]

attestation.note: The stable DOI and theorem locator are supplied in place of a verbatim transcription; the emitted statement is the ray-monotonic integral inequality used below.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the precise classical moving-set inequality used to establish strict Gaussian cube comparison.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited theorem gives weak ray monotonicity; the strict bounded-cube conclusion needed here is derived separately.
added_lemmas.consumer: The strict comparison lemma uses this leaf to compare unequal covariance matrices.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\), \(R>0\), \(C_R=[-R,R]^n\), and \(X\sim N(0,V)\) with \(V\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).  For every nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
 \Pr\{X+u\in C_R\}<\Pr\{X\in C_R\}.
\]
Consequently, if \(U\sim N(0,\Delta)\) is independent of \(X\), where \(\Delta\succeq0\) and \(\Delta\ne0\), then
\[
 \Pr\{X+U\in C_R\}<\Pr\{X\in C_R\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(f_V\) for the everywhere-positive density of \(N(0,V)\), and fix
\(u\ne0\).  The density is symmetric, integrable, and its nonempty
superlevel sets are centered ellipsoids, hence convex.  The cube \(C_R\) is
bounded, convex, symmetric, and has nonempty interior.  Define
\[
 h(t)=\Pr\{X+tu\in C_R\}
     =\int_{C_R}f_V(x-tu)\,dx,
 \qquad t\geq0. \tag{1}
\]
For \(0\leq s\leq t\) with \(t>0\), apply
\texttt{lem:anderson-ray-monotonicity} with \(y=-tu\) and \(k=s/t\).
It gives
\[
 h(s)=\int_{C_R}f_V(x-su)\,dx
 \geq\int_{C_R}f_V(x-tu)\,dx=h(t). \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(h\) is nonincreasing on \([0,\infty)\).

We prove that equality in (2) between zero and a positive shift is
impossible.  Put
\[
 q=u^{\top}V^{-1}u>0,
 \qquad d(x)=u^{\top}V^{-1}x.
\]
Completing the square in the Gaussian density yields, for real \(t\),
\[
 h(t)=e^{-qt^2/2}\int_{C_R}e^{t d(x)}f_V(x)\,dx. \tag{3}
\]
Because \(C_R\) is bounded, \(d\) is bounded on \(C_R\).  Consequently the
power series for the two exponentials in (3) converge uniformly on every
bounded subset of the complex \(t\)-plane and may be integrated term by
term.  Hence the right-hand side of (3) extends to an entire function of
\(t\).

If \(h(1)=h(0)\), monotonicity (2) would give \(h(t)=h(0)\) for every
\(t\in[0,1]\).  An entire function that equals a constant on a real interval
equals that constant everywhere: otherwise, at an accumulation point of its
zeros, the first nonzero coefficient of its convergent power series would
make the zero isolated.  Thus equality would force \(h(t)=h(0)\) for all
real \(t\).

This is impossible.  Let \(\lambda_{\min}(V^{-1})>0\).  Since
\(\lVert x\rVert_2\leq R\sqrt n\) on \(C_R\), for all sufficiently large
\(t\),
\[
 f_V(x-tu)
 \leq (2\pi)^{-n/2}\det(V)^{-1/2}
 exp\!\left[-\frac{\lambda_{\min}(V^{-1})}{2}
       \{t\lVert u\rVert_2-R\sqrt n\}^2\right]. \tag{4}
\]
Integrating (4) over the finite-volume cube gives \(h(t)\to0\), whereas
\(h(0)>0\) because \(f_V>0\) and \(C_R\) has positive volume.  Therefore
\[
 h(1)<h(0), \tag{5}
\]
which proves the first assertion.

For the consequence, \(\Delta\succeq0\) and \(\Delta\ne0\) imply that some
\(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(v^{\top}\Delta v>0\).  Thus
\(v^{\top}U\) is a nondegenerate univariate normal random variable and
\[
 \Pr\{U=0\}\leq\Pr\{v^{\top}U=0\}=0. \tag{6}
\]
Conditioning on \(U\), applying (5) at every realized nonzero shift, and
using independence give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{X+U\in C_R\}
 &=\mathbb E\bigl[\Pr\{X+u\in C_R\}\vert_{u=U}\bigr]\\
 &<\Pr\{X\in C_R\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
The argument permits singular \(\Delta\); positive definiteness is required
only for \(V\).
added_lemmas.justification: Strictness for a bounded cube turns a nonzero Loewner covariance reduction into a strict quantile reduction even when the covariance difference is singular.
added_lemmas.gap: Ordinary Anderson comparison is weak; the analytic equality argument rules out equality for every nonzero Gaussian shift in the setting used here.
added_lemmas.consumer: The correlated exact-frontier theorem uses this lemma at the deep optimizer.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  Suppose \(\mathcal E\ne\varnothing\) and \(L=\delta=0\).  For \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), put
\[
 V(w)=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}.
\]
For every \(V\in\mathbb S_{++}^M\), let \(r_\alpha(V)\) be the unique positive \(R\) satisfying
\[
 \Pr_{Z\sim N(0,V)}\{\lVert Z\rVert_\infty\leq R\}=1-\alpha.
\]
Then \(r_\alpha\) is continuous on \(\mathbb S_{++}^M\), the displayed minimum below is attained, and
\[
 W_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}r_\alpha\!\left(V(w)\right). \tag{6}
\]
Moreover, let \(w_D\) be a minimizer in (6) for the deep rule.  If some \(w_N\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}\) satisfies
\[
 V(w_N)\preceq V(w_D)
 \quad\text{and}\quad V(w_N)\ne V(w_D), \tag{7}
\]
then \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a positive-definite \(M\times M\) matrix \(V\), define
\[
 G_V(R)=\Pr_{Z\sim N(0,V)}\{Z\in[-R,R]^M\},
 \qquad R\geq0. \tag{8}
\]
The Gaussian density is everywhere positive and continuous.  It follows
that \(G_V\) is continuous, \(G_V(0)=0\), and
\(G_V(R)\to1\) as \(R\to\infty\).  If \(0\leq R_1<R_2\), the set
\([-R_2,R_2]^M\setminus[-R_1,R_1]^M\) contains a nonempty open rectangle,
so positivity of the density gives
\[
 G_V(R_1)<G_V(R_2). \tag{9}
\]
Because \(0<\alpha<1/2\), equations (8)--(9) and the intermediate-value
property give a unique \(r_\alpha(V)>0\) with
\(G_V(r_\alpha(V))=1-\alpha\).

We next verify continuity rather than assume it.  If \(V_n\to V\) in
\(\mathbb S_{++}^M\), then for every fixed \(R\), the normal densities with
covariances \(V_n\) converge pointwise on \([-R,R]^M\) to the density with
covariance \(V\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the determinants are
bounded away from zero, so those densities are bounded on the cube by one
integrable constant.  Dominated convergence therefore gives
\[
 G_{V_n}(R)\longrightarrow G_V(R). \tag{10}
\]
Write \(r=r_\alpha(V)\).  For every \(0<\varepsilon<r\), strict
monotonicity gives
\[
 G_V(r-\varepsilon)<1-\alpha<G_V(r+\varepsilon). \tag{11}
\]
By (10), both inequalities in (11) hold with \(V_n\) in place of \(V\) for
all sufficiently large \(n\).  The defining uniqueness and monotonicity of
the quantile then imply
\[
 r-\varepsilon<r_\alpha(V_n)<r+\varepsilon. \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(r_\alpha(V_n)\to r_\alpha(V)\), proving continuity.

Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} gives
\(D_{jK}\ne\varnothing\), and the adoption-time definition gives
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\) for \(0\leq h\leq K\).  Hence every coordinate
simplex under either support rule is nonempty.  Each is a closed and bounded
subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and there are finitely many
coordinates.  Therefore their product \(\mathcal F_s\) is nonempty and
compact.  The entries of \(A(w)\), and hence those of
\[
 V(w)=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}, \tag{13}
\]
are polynomial functions of \(w\).  By
\texttt{lem:contrast-geometry},
\[
 V(w)\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M\succ0 \tag{14}
\]
for every feasible \(w\).  Equations (12)--(14) show that
\(w\mapsto r_\alpha(V(w))\) is continuous on a nonempty compact set, so its
minimum is attained.

It remains to prove that this observed-law functional equals the causal-width
frontier rather than identify them by definition.  Under \(L=\delta=0\),
\texttt{lem:bias-radius} gives, for every feasible \(w\), every coordinate
\(e\), and every law in the model class,
\[
 a_e(w)^{\top}m=0. \tag{15}
\]
By \texttt{lem:prediction-error}, the difference between the observed linear
synthetic-control estimator and the realized causal contrast is therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)-\tau=Z(w),
 \qquad Z(w)\sim N(0,V(w)). \tag{16}
\]
Thus every member of the model class induces the same centered Gaussian
error law in (16); the causal target \(\tau\) remains the potential-outcome
contrast fixed before this calculation.

Fix \(w\), a nonnegative half-width vector \(\ell\), and
\(R=\max_e\ell_e\).  The rectangular event is contained in the cube event:
\[
 \{|Z_e(w)|\leq\ell_e\text{ for every }e\}
 \subseteq\{\lVert Z(w)\rVert_\infty\leq R\}. \tag{17}
\]
If \((w,\ell)\) is honest, (16)--(17) imply
\(G_{V(w)}(R)\geq1-\alpha\), and therefore
\[
 R\geq r_\alpha(V(w)). \tag{18}
\]
Conversely, setting every half-width equal to
\(r_\alpha(V(w))\) makes the two events in (17) equal and gives coverage
exactly \(1-\alpha\) under every model-class law.  Hence the smallest possible
maximum half-width at fixed \(w\) is exactly \(r_\alpha(V(w))\).  Minimizing
over \(w\), and using attainment already proved, establishes (6).

For the strict comparison, write
\[
 V_N=V(w_N),\qquad V_D=V(w_D),\qquad
 \Delta=V_D-V_N. \tag{19}
\]
Condition (7) says \(\Delta\succeq0\) and \(\Delta\ne0\).  By (14),
\(V_N\succ0\).  On a product probability space take independent vectors
\[
 Z_N\sim N(0,V_N),\qquad U\sim N(0,\Delta). \tag{20}
\]
Then \(Z_N+U\sim N(0,V_D)\).  At the positive number
\(R_D=r_\alpha(V_D)\),
\texttt{lem:strict-anderson-gaussian-cube} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 1-\alpha
 &=\Pr\{Z_N+U\in[-R_D,R_D]^M\}\\
 &<\Pr\{Z_N\in[-R_D,R_D]^M\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{21}
\]
Strict monotonicity (9) and the defining root then yield
\[
 r_\alpha(V_N)<R_D=r_\alpha(V_D). \tag{22}
\]
Finally, \(w_D\) is a deep minimizer and \(w_N\) is nested-feasible, so (6)
and (22) imply
\[
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \leq r_\alpha(V_N)
 <r_\alpha(V_D)
 =W_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{23}
\]
No independence among the contrast coordinates, nonsingularity of
\(\Delta\), interiority of a weight vector, or limiting approximation is
used.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem identifies the exact zero-bias width frontier for arbitrary known correlated Gaussian contrasts and gives a strict covariance-order criterion.
added_lemmas.gap: The result optimizes a joint Gaussian-cube quantile over staggered donor simplexes; its strict comparison remains valid for singular covariance increments and degenerate simplex faces.
added_lemmas.consumer: Implementations may minimize the correlated Gaussian maximum quantile directly and obtain a rigorous strict-gap check from a Loewner certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The condition only excludes the vacuous no-target experiment and is a standard domain condition, not a novel modeling assumption.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  Suppose
\(\mathcal E\ne\varnothing\), \(L=\delta=0\), \(\Sigma_Q\) is diagonal, and
the eligible row-cell sets are pairwise disjoint:
\(\mathcal C^s_e\cap\mathcal C^s_f=\varnothing\) whenever \(e\ne f\).
Then every \(v_{s,e}\) is attained and strictly positive, and \(W_s\) is the
unique positive number \(R_s\) satisfying
\[
 \prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{R_s}{\sqrt{v_{s,e}}}\right)-1\right\}
 =1-\alpha. \tag{8}
\]
If the displayed conditions hold for both support rules, then
\(v_{\mathrm{nested},e}\leq v_{\mathrm{deep},e}\) for every
\(e\in\mathcal E\).  If this inequality is strict for at least one
coordinate, then \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
proposed.justification: The theorem supplies an exact, computable frontier on a transparent observable subclass and proves when a strict coordinatewise variance gain forces a strict simultaneous-width gain.
proposed.gap: The donor geometry comes from the staggered design; the Gaussian product-root characterization is specific to this note's bounded-mean known-covariance experiment.
proposed.consumer: Implementations can solve one monotone scalar equation after coordinatewise simplex variance minimization and use the result as an exact calibration check.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but its proof now specializes and consumes the new correlated-Gaussian exact-frontier theorem, so that dependency must be explicit.

prose_updates.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking sets of not-yet-treated donors. Conditional on a nonempty rationally encoded fixed design, this note turns all treated-unit--horizon errors into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector, derives the exact worst-case bias radius, and chooses horizon-specific simplex weights with a fixed-Bonferroni SOCP. The resulting band is finite-sample honest and lies within a dimension-uniform factor of the best deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle. On the zero-bias class, the exact correlated-Gaussian frontier is the minimum over feasible weights of the centered Gaussian-cube quantile, and a nonzero Loewner covariance reduction at a deep optimizer gives a strict nested-width gain. Diagonal covariance with disjoint eligible row cells yields the explicit Gaussian-product root, and the two-horizon witness has a proved strict exact-width gap as well as a strict \(\Gamma\) gap. The facial-reduction theorem separately gives a complete degeneracy-safe if-and-only-if certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply donor geometry only, not this statistical class or an evaluated estimator.

project_justification.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein define the shrinking donor sets and focus their exposition and application on \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors. This note uses that geometry but neither attributes its bounded-mean Gaussian class to them nor claims that either width program evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik supply non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction and conic architecture but do not optimize the exact honest joint width over the two nested products of donor simplexes. Scalar convex-class interval theory does not give the correlated Gaussian-cube variational frontier, its strict Loewner criterion, the independent-coordinate product root, or the degeneracy-safe comparison of the two SOCPs.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance with a prespecified spectral band, rational fixed inputs, a nonempty treated set, and this note's bounded linear conditional-mean class isolate a finite-sample panel decision problem in which donor availability, worst-case bias, shared-cell covariance, multiplicity, and exact comparison are explicit. The targets are the attainable honest-width frontier \(W_s\), its implementable fixed-Bonferroni surrogate \(\Gamma_s\), and auditable strict-improvement tests for each object on its proved domain.
project_justification.fill: The note derives a deduplicated contrast representation, an exact support-function bias radius, finite-sample honest SOCP bands, and a dimension-uniform comparison with the exact robust frontier. It characterizes \(W_s\) on the zero-bias correlated-Gaussian class as an attained covariance-quantile optimization, proves a strict Loewner covariance criterion, specializes it to an explicit independent-coordinate product root, proves a strict exact-width gain in the rational staggered witness, and proves a separate finite if-and-only-if facial-reduction certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on degenerate active faces.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs. On the zero-bias class, the general correlated exact frontier is characterized through the known-covariance Gaussian-cube quantile; numerical correlated Gaussian-max calibration remains a post-solve refinement. The diagonal row-disjoint specialization reduces calibration to one explicit product equation.

prose_updates.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2, paragraphs defining \(\mathcal D_{jk}\)) provide the shrinking-donor-set geometry and focus their exposition and application on the deepest pool \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may instead use horizon-varying donor sets. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates or dominates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; the present frontier changes the decision variable and loss. Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak ray-monotonic moving-set inequality; this note derives the strict bounded-cube consequence for a nonzero, possibly singular covariance increment and applies it to the optimized staggered-donor frontier. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2 and 3) supply Gaussian comparison tools for the general constant-factor result, while the global spectral covariance band is this note's explicit finite-experiment restriction. Pataki (2013, Sections 3--4), Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1), and exact real-algebraic elimination support the proved degeneracy-safe certificate theorem \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\). Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026), Cerulli (2024), and Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) address different prediction, long-panel, donor-selection, or calibration regimes.
prose_updates.interpretation: The strict witness isolates the value of an early donor that is untreated when the early effect is measured but adopts by the final horizon. Allowing that donor only where valid lowers the early minimum variance from \(3/2\) to \(4/3\) without changing the late variance \(3/200\). The exact Gaussian-product characterization converts that local variance reduction into a proved strict simultaneous-width reduction, without relying on a numerical interval certificate. More generally, a nested feasible covariance that is strictly smaller in Loewner order than the deep optimum yields a strict exact-width gain even with correlated contrasts and a singular covariance difference. These are statements about deterministic linear bands in the declared experiment, not about the numerical output or statistical class of an existing partially pooled synthetic-control estimator.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact robust frontier \(W_s\) and the implementable SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) remain distinct. On the zero-bias class, the correlated frontier now has an attained Gaussian-cube quantile characterization and a strict Loewner-order criterion; computing general correlated Gaussian-max quantiles remains a post-solve refinement. The rational witness proves strict improvement for both objects through the diagonal row-disjoint specialization. Outside covariance comparability at a deep optimizer, the paper proves weak support dominance and the dimension-uniform comparison, not that every strict \(\Gamma\) gap is a strict \(W\) gap. The facial-reduction equivalence \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\) concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate active faces.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample coverage, the covariance-domination sandwich, the constant-factor frontier, weak nested-support dominance, and the two-horizon strict witness are theorem-level results. On the zero-bias class, \(\texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier}\) gives an attained exact-width variational formula and a strict Loewner covariance criterion. On its diagonal row-disjoint specialization, \(\texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier}\) gives the explicit product root, and \(\texttt{prop:strict-witness-exact-frontier-gap}\) gives a proved positive exact-width gap. The complete finite certificate on degenerate SOCP faces is proved by \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\); it is not an open OEQ and is not a substitute for exact-\(W\) strictness. The covariance band is a prespecified restriction for the known-covariance finite experiment. Unknown covariance, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, numerical general correlated Gaussian-max calibration, and a direct comparison with the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein partially pooled estimator are outside this version. When donor sets coincide, the two support rules reduce to the same problem; with one unbiased contrast, the SOCP reduces to a rationally certified classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition turns the exact product-root comparison into a proved positive exact-width gap for the rational witness; no numerical interval certificate is required.
statement_notes.consumer: The rational variance vectors and root equations provide a structural independent-Gaussian calibration check for \(\texttt{scpi}\) and \(\texttt{augsynth::multisynth}\).
